I attached our questionnaire (short PDF). Can you respond by EOD Thursday? Please loop in whoever owns Support Ops and Compliance.

Vivek / team — drafting the answers inline below and attaching the on-call rotation example. I'm keeping responses concise for the RFI; happy to expand where you see fit.

1) TAM coverage model- Redwood provides a named Technical Account Manager (TAM) for enterprise contracts. Standard TAM coverage: business hours coverage (US PST 8am–6pm local customer hours) with 24x7 on-call escalation handled by Support Engineering for P1s. For global customers we offer a follow-the-sun TAM add-on that pairs regional TAMs to guarantee daytime coverage across regions.

2) On-call duty rotation and handovers- Support Engineering maintains a two-week on-call rotation; TAMs are not typically on 24x7 by default (unless contracted). Handovers: the outgoing engineer fills a handover note in a dedicated Confluence page and updates the shared on-call roster (see attached CS_Oncall_Rotation_Example.xlsx). Handover checklist items: active incidents, outstanding customer callbacks with timestamps, known workarounds, and any scheduled maintenance windows. Handover must be completed in the hour prior to shift change and acknowledged by the incoming on-call. All handovers are timestamped and retained.

3) Incident notification cadence and stakeholder tiers- We use a tiered notification model:
  - P1 (service unavailable / data loss): 15-minute detection -> 30-minute initial notification to customer TAM and security contact -> hourly updates until mitigation. Post-incident root cause analysis (RCA) delivered within 5 business days (initial technical summary within 24 hours).
  - P2 (degraded service): initial notification within 60 minutes -> updates every 4 hours until resolved. RCA within 10 business days.
  - P3 (minor): notification in regular business hours; weekly summary if multiple small events.

Notification channels: email + PagerDuty for P1/P2, optional SMS for executive contacts. Templates attached in the incident packet.

4) Audit log retention for incident records- We retain incident records, postmortems, and associated logs in our audit archive for 5 years by default. For customers requiring longer retention (e.g., 7 years), we offer configurable archival exports or dedicated longer-retention buckets as part of the enterprise contract. Data exports can be delivered as encrypted S3 objects with customer-supplied KMS key options. See attached audit-retention-summary-2025.pdf for a table of artifacts (incident timeline, incident communications, RCA, change requests) and default retention windows.

5) Ownership and sharing of postmortems- Primary ownership: Support Engineering produces the technical RCA; TAM drafts the customer-facing postmortem. Delivery SLA: initial customer-facing postmortem draft within 5 business days for P1s; final postmortem within 10 business days. Postmortems are shared via secure link (signed URL or shared Drive) and optionally uploaded to the customer's Jira/SNOW instance via automation.

Notes / exceptions:
- For regulated customers requiring formal audit packages, we will include additional forensic artifacts under an amended SOW.
- For retention beyond 7 years, we coordinate a custom archival policy and associated cost in the contract.

Attachments: CS_Oncall_Rotation_Example.xlsx (roster + sample handover notes), incident-templates.txt (P1/P2/P3 templates), audit-retention-summary-2025.pdf

Marissa — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple quick clarifying questions so we can include accurate language in our vendor risk matrix: 

1) For the handover notes you mentioned — is there an API or export for the handover history, or is it maintained as Confluence pages only? We need an audit-friendly export of handover logs.
2) When you say "incident records" are retained 5 years by default, can you confirm whether the raw KV cache traces and ephemeral model inputs used for debugging are included in that retention? Our legal team is strict about PII in logs.
3) For the P1 notification SLA (15-minute detection -> 30-minute initial notification) — do you have historical SLAs/metrics you can share for the past 12 months? We don't need raw logs, just rolling SLA compliance numbers (percent on-time notifications).

If you can respond inline we'll move rapidly; otherwise a short call Friday is fine.

Thanks,
Sabrina

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Hi Sabrina — quick answers below (following Marissa's high-level replies). I'm Support Eng and own our incident artifacts / exports.

1) Handover export: We keep handover notes in Confluence and sync structured metadata to an internal on-call service (audit logs accessible via API). For enterprise customers we can provision a read-only export endpoint or provide S3-delivered CSV exports of the handover history on request. This export includes timestamps, on-call assignee, acknowledged flag, and free-text summary.

2) Raw KV cache & ephemeral inputs: By default we do not persist raw ephemeral model inputs beyond short-term debugging TTLs (48–72 hours) in the serving layer. For customers requiring longer persistence for debugging, we offer an opt-in capture that streams traces to a secured archive under the customer's retention policy; this is contractually gated and flagged for PII handling. We redact or pseudonymize PII by default; if raw inputs are required we provide secure transfer under a signed Data Handling Addendum and KMS-controlled storage.

3) SLA metrics: Our operational dashboards show 12-month rolling notification compliance. For P1 notification on-time rate we are currently at 98.6% (rolling 12 months), with mean time to initial notification at 22 minutes. We can provide an anonymized monthly breakdown as part of the procurement packet.

I've attached the short SLA-compliance extract and the API spec for the handover export. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call Friday to walk these details through.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
